distractors: Written in unnecessarily technical language, so that a general reader stalls on the vocabulary rather than the argument.
Delivered so fast that nobody can follow it, the argument fine on the page and gone by the time you look up from your notes.

Deliberately vague so as to avoid committing to anything, phrased so that either outcome can afterwards be read as the one that was meant. The evasion is the point of it, and it can be managed in very few words.

Formal to the point of coldness, correct in every particular and offering the reader nothing at all to hold on to. It is a complaint about the temperature of the writing rather than about how much of it there is.

Full of confident claims with nothing standing behind any of them, so that the register stays certain and the evidence never arrives. What is wrong is the gap between the assurance and the support, which a short paragraph manages as easily as a long one.
